title: Multi-Signal Fallback Orchestrator for Region and Tier Routing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a centralized runtime component (Fallback Orchestrator) that uses multiple runtime signals to trigger automatic fallbacks and circuit-breaker actions for region selection and tier routing. The orchestrator should ingest 429 spike events, timeout ratios, error-rate windows, P95/P99 latency heatmaps, and model-variant quality regressions to decide when to route traffic to alternate regions, lower-cost tiers, or compatible fallback model variants. It must respect customer tier priorities, region affinity, and active rollout policies, and expose observability hooks and a safe rollout plan for production. This ticket covers the algorithm, runtime integration, metrics, rollout, and a basic runbook for operator intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator computes a single 'fallback signal score' per route-region-tier every 10s using 429, timeout ratio, error rate, and latency, exposed in metrics (prometheus metrics names: fallback_score_total, fallback_action_count)

When score exceeds dynamic threshold, orchestrator triggers one of: (a) route to fallback model variant, (b) shift traffic to next tier, or (c) regional cutover with hysteresis and cooldown — actions are logged and visible in Console rollout UI
Circuit-breaker prevents oscillation via per-route cooldown windows and decaying trip score; observed oscillation rate must be < 1% during chaos test
Respect customer 'tier pin' and VIP flags: if customer has explicit pin to model/version/region, orchestrator logs action as 'blocked-by-pin' and not reroutes without manual approval
End-to-end integration tests simulate 429 burst, model error spike, and regional capacity loss — orchestrator executes expected fallback path within SLA (action latency < 30s) and records audit event
Runbook describing manual override, rollback, and post-incident analysis is created and linked in ticket
steps: Design and finalize scoring function (weighting defaults + config overrides) — include initial weights for signals and risk multipliers for customer tier
Add Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry traces for signals ingestion, score computation, and actions
Implement orchestrator service with pluggable policy engine and persistent trip-state storage (per-route TTL + decay)
Integrate orchestrator with router: callbacks to change routing table or set per-request policy override
Add feature flag gated rollout (start in a single region + canary tenants) and build Console controls for observing/tracing actions
Create unit and e2e chaos tests, QA runbook, and on-call playbook entries
notes: Scoring function uses exponentially-weighted moving averages over 10s/30s/5m windows to capture bursts and sustained degradation
Prefer circuit-breaker action ordering: 1) fallback model variant (same region), 2) lower tier within region, 3) regional handover — this minimizes latency and compliance/regulatory impact
We will allow per-customer override config stored in customer metadata service; defaults are global and adjustable via Console
Trade-off: aggressive thresholds reduce customer impact but increase cost (more fallbacks to higher-priced variants). Will monitor cost delta and add budget caps per account if needed
Security: all orchestrator actions must emit audit events and tie to operator IDs for compliance
If region handover occurs, we must preserve KV cache affinity where possible; otherwise expect cold-cache latency penalty — notify Console
